html:
Cyclone Heta struck Niue in January 2004 with very strong winds and huge waves that washed over the cliffs. It wrecked much of the capital, Alofi, on the island's west coast.

Homes, government buildings and the national museum, with many of Niue's historic objects, were destroyed or badly damaged. New Zealand and Australia sent relief, and the capital was partly rebuilt on higher ground.

Heta hit an island that was already losing people to New Zealand. Some families who lost their homes left for good, adding to the Niuean diaspora. The storm also struck Tonga and American Samoa.
